ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Preventive Visit — Emily Dickinson — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Ms. Dickinson is a 54-year-old woman with stage G3a A2 chronic kidney disease and hypertension who comes to the clinic for her periodic preventive visit, three weeks after her six-month kidney review by video. She chose a quiet first appointment of the morning and asked that her vaccines, cervical screening, and mammogram be done on this one trip; her second hepatitis B dose was held for today for the same reason. She completed the health risk assessment at home and sent it in beforehand. She has had no headaches for several months. She takes losartan 100 mg, dapagliflozin 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, and vitamin D3 daily, and she has taken no NSAIDs. She has had no illness since the gastroenteritis in April. Her home blood pressure averages 118/72. She writes most mornings and works in her garden most afternoons. [S]

Follow-up: Mammogram straight after this visit. Return the stool test kit within two weeks. Zoster dose 2 and the COVID-19 vaccine at a home visit in two to six months. Yearly kidney tests and review in January. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She named a health care agent from her household and completed a health care proxy form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. She said that what matters most to her is staying in her own home, keeping her privacy, and being able to write. She wants full treatment for reversible illness, with care at home whenever it is safe. She would not want dialysis started without a frank discussion of what it would mean for her daily life, and she asked for information about conservative kidney care for the future. She chose not to record other specific treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly and at any change in kidney function. [S]
